text:
The unit vector that fixes the measurement direction in the \(x\hbox{–}z\) plane can be written  
\[
\mathbf n = (\sin\theta,\,0,\,\cos\theta),\qquad 0\le\theta\le\pi .
\]

The spin-(or here, “\(\vec P\)–”) operator along this direction is  

\[
P_{\mathbf n}= \mathbf n\cdot\vec P
           = \sin\theta\,P_x+\cos\theta\,P_z
           =\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\sin\theta\,\sigma_x+\cos\theta\,\sigma_z\bigr),
\]
where  
\(\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\;
  \sigma_z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}\).

Hence, in the basis of \(\sigma_z\) eigenstates,

\[
\frac{2}{\hbar}P_{\mathbf n}= 
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\[2pt]
\sin\theta & -\cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

We need the eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue \(+\hbar/2\) (i.e. eigenvalue \(+1\) of the dimensionless matrix above).  
Let the eigenvector be \(v=(a,b)^{T}\).  Then  

\[
(\cos\theta-1)a+\sin\theta\,b = 0.
\]

For \(\sin\theta\neq 0\),

\[
\frac{b}{a}= \frac{1-\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}
           = \frac{2\sin^{2}(\theta/2)}{2\sin(\theta/2)\cos(\theta/2)}
           = \tan\frac{\theta}{2}.
\]

Choosing a normalization where \(a=\cos(\theta/2)\) gives \(b=\sin(\theta/2)\).  
Because \(\cos^{2}(\theta/2)+\sin^{2}(\theta/2)=1\), this vector is already normalized:

\[
\boxed{\;|+\mathbf n\rangle = 
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos(\theta/2)\\[2pt]
\sin(\theta/2)
\end{pmatrix}\; }.
\]

This matches option (B).

Answer: B
